behaviorToPreserve: In progress is independent of completion and numeric priority; retain the existing short double-click toggle
Hold mouse or Space for one second to toggle completion; show no completed checkmark before the threshold
Cancel an incomplete hold on release, pointer exit, capture loss, scrolling, lost focus, hiding or disabling
Due soon means within 24 hours, overdue means at or before now, and later deadlines are scheduled
Completed tasks have no active due-warning state; keep their stored deadline information available
State labels and icons supplement color; preserve accessible task names and keyboard operation
taskStatesExploration.notes: User selected option 1 Quiet Ledger for the normal Classic Todo theme and option 4 Pixel Signals for Pixel Voyage, including each option's matching hold feedback. Quiet Ledger uses inline status/date cues and a thin progress line; Pixel Signals uses stepped status labels and a segmented hold meter. Soft Labels and Margin Signals remain exploration history only. The lower HOLD FEEDBACK strips are explanatory snapshots, not permanent controls. Short dates are illustrative; implementation must retain the complete deadline including year and time through visible text or accessible detail. Existing behavior and approved row/priority defaults are unchanged. No runtime changes.

behaviorToPreserve: Task context menu retains Edit task, Add > Note/Subtask, conditional Link/Relink, and Delete
Link/Relink appears only when Telegram is enabled; already-linked tasks use Relink
Priority menu keeps all ten levels, with 1 highest; selected-item styling must reflect the actual task value
Editor keeps one multiline task-body field, priority 1-10, and optional local due date/time with Clear
Manual position Top/Bottom appears only for new Todos, never while editing an existing Todo
Checklist editor retains completion, editable text, move up/down, remove, and Add subtask controls
Save versus Save changes, Ctrl+Enter, Escape, close, focus, scrolling and resizing remain functional
Preserve validation, save failures and sync warnings, and the existing task deletion confirmation and scope text
Standalone note/subtask editors retain their simpler text-only mode; do not add parent priority or deadline controls to them
taskMenusAndEditorsExploration.notes: User approved both coordinated design sheets for their corresponding normal Classic and Pixel Voyage themes. Numbers identify surfaces rather than four competing styles. Approved Classic surfaces use quiet parchment, gently rounded corners and thin brass; Pixel surfaces use the same palette with small stepped outlines. The Add example has the optional deadline disabled; the Edit example shows it enabled, without changing either mode's capabilities. Menu examples show Add open and priority 3 selected. Artwork colors are illustrative; retain the existing priority palette and data. Standalone detail dialogs, deletion confirmations and error/empty states are not newly designed by these boards. No runtime implementation or new Settings defaults.

boards.additionalSamples: Classic and Pixel inline Telegram retry notices

behaviorToPreserve: Distinguish no saved todos from all tasks completed; the all-done sample has Show completed off
Unconfigured notes folders and read failures must retain their own messages, never masquerade as empty or completed lists
Save failures retain editable input and the existing Save action; do not show a saved-success state
Saved locally with a sync warning keeps the saved task and uses the existing Close action; do not save it again or imply undo
Show automatic Telegram retry text only for the existing retry state, not for every sync warning
Delete confirmation preserves the actual task excerpt, linked or unlinked deletion scope, and irreversible-action warning
Compact note/subtask editors remain multiline text-only forms with Save, Cancel, Ctrl+Enter and Escape
Keep real validation and service messages available and wrapped; mockup wording is illustrative, not a replacement for all errors
supportingStatesAndDialogsExploration.approvedPresentationRefinement: After a successful local save with a sync warning, show one Close action and Esc to Close instead of the redundant Cancel action and save-oriented hint. Reuse the existing saved-warning close behavior; no retry or undo feature is proposed.
supportingStatesAndDialogsExploration.notes: User approved all three coordinated design sheets for the corresponding Classic and Pixel Voyage themes. The feedback sheet contains footer close-ups, not replacement editor forms; the rest of the approved fields remain. The delete example is for a task with a linked Telegram message; unlinked tasks and detail deletion retain their corresponding scope text. Compact Add subtask and Edit note use the same text-only form as the illustrated Add note and Edit subtask. These are approved design references, with no production code or Settings changes.

appearanceSettingsExploration.scope: Todo overlay appearance only; other settings categories and application/clock appearance remain separate
proposedBehavior: Use the approved initial selections on first activation and remember later customizations separately for Classic and Pixel Voyage
Keep all retained row, priority, detail, toolbar, background and emblem alternatives available in either style
Keep task feedback tied to the user-selected theme mapping: Quiet Ledger for Classic, Pixel Signals for Pixel Voyage
Engraved header toggles only header map decoration, without changing the selected emblem or body background
Update sample-data preview and the Todo appearance immediately after applying a choice, following the existing Settings interaction model; Done closes Settings
Preview uses sample tasks and cannot modify real tasks, notes or synchronization data
Each emblem picker stages a choice; Use emblem applies only its invoking header or launcher target; Cancel and close discard the staged choice
Render the selected launcher emblem as a transparent standalone logo regardless of background selection
Keep the right-side controls scrollable at smaller window sizes; scale preview artwork uniformly and keep menu labels readable
Persistence failures must be visible and controls must reflect the actual applied state, without silent reversion
appearanceSettingsExploration.notes: Two raster design previews awaiting review, not interactive Settings implementation. The page shows Classic and Navigator Parchment selected. Four backgrounds are thumbnails, two emblem selectors open the shared sixteen-logo picker, and four dropdowns expose only the retained alternatives. The picker depicts the header target; the launcher target reuses the layout with appropriate title. Settings selection-cell outlines are not part of the emblem or launcher artwork. Source emblems remain custom reference interpretations; individual transparent assets still require production preparation and small-size review. The visible sample contains the approved Classic details and a separate transparent launcher preview. No changes to production settings or saved user preferences.
